verdicts.method: REPRODUCE: for r in architecture-docs archon aiur: jq -r '.topic_class' ~/.aiur/repo/aiur-team/$r/executor/$r.executor.wakes.ndjson | sort | uniq -c; wc -l on each file; jq -r '[.topic_class,(.needs_attention|tostring),.count]|@tsv' for the capacity/prewarm classes. INTERPRET: compared each wake_id to <repo>.executor.wakes.cursor.json and executor.claims.json; computed first_seen_at cadence and per-day counts with python; read the snapshot's Aiur.ExecutorWakeInbox (2 s debounce, coalesces only on the same {topic_class, ticket} key) and agent_control_cli executor-wait (returns every unread record at once); read git log for the fixes #2434 (2026-08-23) and #2622 (2026-09-10); tallied capacity classes in the aiur stream after 2026-09-11 and in the khala stream.
verdicts.note: The counts match exactly: architecture-docs has 1,067 of 1,881 lines (56.7%), archon has 523 of 810 (64.6%), and aiur has 515 + 500 = 1,015 of 4,749 (21.4%). Every capacity.starved and prewarm_blocked line has needs_attention=true and count=1. The .resolved lines have needs_attention=false. The 'noise' label is supported: the capacity.starved lines are periodic re-announcements of one ongoing, ticketless condition. They arrive every ~67 s (architecture-docs) and every ~125 s (archon), with no .resolved line between them, so the 2 s debounce never merges them. Fix #2622 (#2592) says they were false starvation: dependency-held backlog that 'no added capacity could ever satisfy'. The prewarm pair flapped from blocked to resolved in a median of 124 s. Three problems weaken the conclusion. (1) 'The Executor has to read' is overstated. The architecture-docs owner cursor stopped at wake 352 (2026-09-03 22:49Z), and its claims file lists no consumer, so 906 of 1,067 starved lines (85%) were never acknowledged by an Executor. In archon, the cursor stopped at 546 and 124 of 523 were never acknowledged. (2) The counts come from short windows before the fixes, not from steady state. The starved bursts are 2026-09-03..04 and 09-09..10, ending just before #2622 merged (2026-09-11 02:30Z). The prewarm pair falls only in 2026-08-18..08-24, stops right after #2434 'Only alert on persistent prewarm holds' (08-23), and never recurs. After 09-11, the aiur stream has 269 lines with almost no capacity wakes. The khala stream (09-16..09-26, 2,247 lines) has 73 capacity-class lines (3.2%), of which 31 are starved (1.4%). (3) A line is not an Executor turn, because one executor-wait call returns every unread record in one batch. So these numbers overstate how much dedup or suppression is worth for current code.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the historical streams, capacity-class wakes did dominate: capacity.starved is 57% of architecture-docs (1,067/1,881) and 65% of archon (523/810), and the prewarm_blocked/.resolved pair is 21% of aiur (1,015/4,749). All starved and blocked lines are needs_attention=true and count=1. But these are bursts from two bugs that are now fixed. The starved lines are false-starvation re-announcements every ~1-2 minutes on 2026-09-03..04 and 09-09..10, fixed by #2622. The prewarm flapping falls on 2026-08-18..24 only, fixed by #2434. An owning Executor never acknowledged most architecture-docs starved lines (906/1,067 are past the cursor) or 124 of the archon ones. In the current streams, capacity wakes are about 3% (khala: 73/2,247; starved 31). Treat them as evidence that alerts can repeat without coalescing, not as the present Executor reading load.

verdicts.method: REPRODUCE: find ~/.aiur/repo/aiur-team/khala/executor/handoffs -name '*handoff*.md' | sort, then python parsing the filename UTC stamps for per-day counts, median gap and gaps under 10 min; same for aiur. Session counts: python over the first line (session_meta) of ~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl with cwd == <local-checkouts>/khala; ~/.claude/history.jsonl sessionIds for that project; the transcript dir listing. INTERPRET: wc -c and diff between successive khala handoffs; parsed the one khala Claude transcript (b7aada0d...jsonl) for Bash tool_use inputs that touch handoffs/*handoff.md and for compact_boundary events; read the installed aiur-run and aiur-handoff skill text on archiving.
verdicts.note: The numbers match: 61 files (09-17: 1, 09-18: 58, 09-20: 2), median gap 4.4 min, 45 gaps under 10 min. The two 09-20 files share one timestamp, and one of them is the 'previous-live-handoff-with-session-log' copy. aiur has 18 handoffs, median gap 48.7 min, 3 gaps under 10 min. khala has one Claude session (history and transcripts both give only b7aada0d, first event 2026-09-18 00:52Z) and one top-level codex-tui session (2026-09-16, thread 01a0ab55, plus 7 subagent threads and 1 codex_exec). 'Not 58 real Executor changes' is correct. 'Handoff loop or Executor thrash' is not the best reading. All 58 files from 09-18 are successive snapshots of one document, written by one Claude session. The header 'Claude takeover ... replaced Codex thread 01a0ab55' is the same in each, and the size grows steadily from 2,470 B to 35,097 B. All 57 successive diffs are pure appends (0 lines removed), each adding a '## Update HH:MMZ' section. The transcript has 58 deliberate Bash calls of the form: cat >> handoff.md <<EOF ## Update ...; cp handoff.md handoffs/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-handoff.md. Each call has new content, so no automated trigger fired them. They are not per-compaction: the session's first compaction is at 11:07Z, after the last 09-18 handoff at 10:59Z. The cause is guidance, not a loop. aiur-run says 'Keep executor/handoff.md current for the whole run' and also 'write a new, timestamped document... Never overwrite an archived handoff', and the Executor archived every running update. aiur shows the same pattern on a smaller scale: its 9 handoffs on 09-16 are also append-only snapshots of one Codex Executor's document. So the khala-vs-aiur comparison is a difference of degree, not of kind. The khala data shows about one real Executor transition, Codex to Claude on 2026-09-18 ~01:10Z.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The khala Executor wrote 61 handoff files (58 on 2026-09-18, median gap 4.4 min, 45 gaps under 10 min), but they do not come from a loop or from Executor thrash. The 58 files on 09-18 are append-only checkpoint snapshots of one running handoff document, written by the single Claude Executor session (b7aada0d). Each snapshot came from a deliberate 'append ## Update HH:MMZ; cp handoff.md handoffs/<UTC>-handoff.md' tool call. There was no compaction or automated trigger, and the first compaction came at 11:07Z, after the last snapshot. The only real Executor transition in the data is Codex to Claude on 09-18 ~01:10Z. aiur's 18 handoffs contain the same pattern (its 9 on 09-16 are append-only snapshots), so handoff-file counts measure checkpoint frequency, not Executor turnover, in both repos. The cause is ambiguous skill guidance: 'keep handoff.md current' is mixed with 'archive a new timestamped file, never overwrite'. It is not a mechanism that needs a loop guard.

verdicts.method: REPRODUCE: gh api repos/<r> --jq '[.id,.full_name]' for aiur-team/architecture-docs, aiur-team/archon, its-everdred/aiur, aiur-team/aiur; find ~/.aiur/repo -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2 -type d; count of numeric dirs under ~/code/aiur-workspaces/{its-everdred,aiur-team}/aiur; python over session_meta cwd prefixes of all 6,534 ~/.codex/sessions files (old aiur path, misrooted khala path); counted Claude project dirs -aiur-workspaces-aiur-team-{architecture-docs,archon}-N. INTERPRET: read the snapshot's Aiur.Executor.StatePaths.resolve_dir (the state dir comes from the configured GitHub slug via RepoBase.executor_path) and RepoBase.remove_obsolete_aiur_node (a hard-coded aiur-only cleanup of ~/.aiur/repo/its-everdred/aiur); checked the dates of the old-path sessions and overlap between old and new ticket numbers.
verdicts.note: The facts reproduce. architecture-docs and archon both return id 1355265471 with full_name aiur-team/archon. its-everdred/aiur and aiur-team/aiur both return id 1241902373. ~/.aiur/repo/aiur-team has separate architecture-docs and archon dirs with separate wake streams: 09-03..09-05 and 09-09..09-11. Claude transcript namespaces are separate too: 44 architecture-docs-N and 27 archon-N project dirs. ~/code/aiur-workspaces/its-everdred/aiur has 28 ticket dirs, and aiur-team/aiur has 321. 303 Codex sessions have cwd under the old path (106 top-level, 197 subagent). The misrooted ~/.aiur/workspaces/khala/aiur-team/khala has 26 Codex sessions (6 top-level, 20 subagent). The snapshot code turns the inference into a direct observation: StatePaths keys Executor state by the configured slug, and the only rename handling is a special case hard-coded for aiur's org transfer. Nothing merges the architecture-docs and archon state. Caveats that narrow the claim but do not overturn it: (a) for aiur, only workspaces and Codex cwd are split. There is no its-everdred/aiur state dir, because the hard-coded cleanup removes it. All 303 old-path sessions fall on 2026-07-30..07-31, and 12 of the 28 old-path ticket numbers also have dirs under the new path. (b) 'Likewise' mixes a rename (architecture-docs to archon) with an owner transfer (its-everdred to aiur-team). (c) The khala misroot is one root holding sessions from 6 ticket dirs (10-13, 50, 51), all on 2026-09-16, the day the repo was created. It is most likely a workspace.root config artifact, not evidence of name keying.
